# Results — Study 787 (Heatwave-Utilities)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**utilities (XLU) rally through peak-summer heat**: the hottest weeks drive record
air-conditioning load, so (folklore says) hold the sector across the dog-days. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Fingerprint `7e03507631b7`
(XLU + SPY, one combined panel, adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `XLU` (Utilities Select Sector SPDR) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 6,921 rows, 1998-12-22 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 27 peak-summer anchors 1999→2025, each a fixed **July 22** — the climatological centre of US peak heat (~4-5 week *seasonal temperature lag* after the June-21 solstice; NOAA / NWS). Identical every year, not a data-mined "hottest day" |
| Events resolvable | all **27** of 27 summers have XLU+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (XLU − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: the peak-heat anchor is a fixed calendar date. Into-heat = [anchor−K → anchor]; past-peak = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Beta, named:** XLU is a low-beta (~0.3-0.5) defensive sector, so a raw XLU move over any
summer window is only weakly market-driven. We still quote the *abnormal* return `XLU − SPY`
so a summer that was simply a strong tape for everything is netted out.

## Into the heat — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE the peak-heat anchor (XLU − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week into-heat (k=10) | 27 | −0.216% | −0.410 | 13/27 = 48.1% [30.7%, 66.0%] |
| 1-month into-heat (k=21) | 27 | −0.194% | −0.331 | 15/27 = 55.6% [37.3%, 72.4%] |

The ramp *into* peak heat is a **clean zero** — both cuts are slightly negative and
statistically indistinguishable from SPY (|*t*| < 0.5, hit rates straddling 50%).

## Through / past the heat — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER the peak-heat anchor

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week past-peak (k=10) | 27 | +0.367% | +0.559 | 14/27 = 51.9% [34.0%, 69.3%] |
| 1-month past-peak (k=21) | 27 | +0.718% | +0.814 | 14/27 = 51.9% [34.0%, 69.3%] |

The "rally through the heat" half is *directionally* right — XLU beats SPY by a whisker in
the late-July-into-August window — but the effect is **far too small to matter**: the
best cut is +0.72% with *t* = +0.81 and a coin-flip 14/27 hit rate. This is noise.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week into-heat | right | −0.216% | −0.032% (0.604%) | 0.6228 |
| 2-week past-peak | right | +0.367% | −0.032% (0.604%) | 0.2535 |

Both observed means sit **well inside the luck cloud** — the past-peak window's +0.37% is
a right-tail p = 0.25 (one random 2-week XLU-vs-SPY window in four is at least this good),
and the into-heat window is dead-centre. Nothing here is outside ordinary tracking noise.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 1-month past-peak *t*

Full-sample *t* = **+0.814**; across all 27 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[+0.365, +1.092]** — the (already-insignificant) tilt is broad rather than one-year
driven, but it never approaches significance in any sub-sample.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month past-peak | +0.718% (*t* +0.81) | +0.618% (*t* +0.70) | +0.518% (*t* +0.59) |
| 1-month into-heat | −0.194% (*t* −0.33) | −0.294% (*t* −0.50) | −0.394% (*t* −0.67) |

The most-favourable window earns +0.72%/yr gross before costs and *t* never clears 1.
After a couple of round-trips of cost it fades further. There is no edge to bank.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = +0.20 (sd 0.94); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **1/20** seeds —
  the detector is well-behaved and quiet on the null at n = 27 events.
- **Planted into-heat run-up +1.0% (seed 814):** mean AR +1.570%, *t* = **+2.09**.
- **Planted into-heat run-up +2.0% (seed 814):** mean AR +2.570%, *t* = **+3.43** — a real
  bump is recovered monotonically. The machinery *would* see a heat rally if one existed.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | No window separates from noise. Into-heat is a slightly-negative zero (|*t*| < 0.5); the "rally through the heat" past-peak window is directionally positive but tiny (+0.72%, *t* = +0.81, placebo right-tail p = 0.25, coin-flip 14/27 hit rate) and never significant in any sub-sample. The synthetic control confirms the detector *would* have caught a real ≥1% seasonal rally — there just isn't one. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. The best cut is +0.72%/yr gross, *t* < 1, decaying with costs, inside a 4-window search — a curiosity, not a strategy. |

**In one sentence:** the "hold utilities through the dog-days of summer" trade is folklore —
XLU's abnormal return across the peak-heat weeks is a directionally-friendly but
statistically empty +0.72% (*t* = +0.81, placebo p = 0.25), indistinguishable from any
random fortnight and gone the moment you charge costs.
